notes: Identity checked from supplied canonical text: title On the effectiveness of self-paced learning; Jonathan G. Tullis and Aaron S. Benjamin; Journal of Memory and Language 64 (2011), 109–118; doi:10.1016/j.jml.2010.11.002. This is the original journal article (author personal copy), including methods, results and references, not an abstract or secondary report. No PDF path supplied; no rendering performed. 35 discrepancy reducers + 39 discrepancy increasers = 74 self-paced participants; each has one yoked control, giving 74 self-paced + 74 fixed-rate controls = 148 participants, organized as 74 paired analytic units. These exhaustive positive/negative allocation groups are described as the subsets of self-paced subjects. This also matches the explicitly printed participant count. No N inferred from degrees of freedom. The superscript-like 1 after [73] in canonical text points to footnote 1 explaining pairwise yoking; it is not part of the degrees of freedom. The article supplies a significance threshold and calls this test significant; .05 is an upper bound, not an exact p. Unassigned replication and success fields are placeholders.
